data.narrative:
Genespire, a Series B biotech company founded by Luigi Naldini and Alessio Cantore, is evaluated against a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage companies in Biotech & Health, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and New Limit.

Two valuation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to Genespire's $52M total raised and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yields $99M. Peer-median triangulation across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a median valuation of $3.8B, with a range spanning $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp P/S anchoring was not applied; the sector median multiple is 7.4x across three public tickers, but Genespire's revenue is not disclosed, precluding this method.

The triangulated range is $84M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $1.9B across both methods. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful uncertainty: stage-progression conservatively extrapolates from capital deployed, while peer-median reflects considerable variation in how capital efficiency and market timing manifest across the biotech frontier-tech cohort. Resolution depends on commercial traction, IP defensibility, and nearness to inflection milestones typical of Series C advancement in the sector.
